LESSON: FOOTBALL

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade five
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS
Strand: Creating and Executing
Topic 1.2: Football
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 18

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Football, part of Creating and Executing in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade five CREATIVE ARTS.

Key inquiry question: Why is the football game popular? 2. What are the advantages of casting with papier mâché?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. execute the skills of kicking, stopping and dribbling in football,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Football in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. prepare papier mâché for casting cones

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Football in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. cast marking cones using papier mâché for football game,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Football in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. enjoy playing a mini game of football in a field marked using coloured cones.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Football in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. execute the skills of kicking, stopping and dribbling in football,

   Football helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. prepare papier mâché for casting cones

   Football helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. cast marking cones using papier mâché for football game,

   Football helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. enjoy playing a mini game of football in a field marked using coloured cones.

   Football helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

E. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. observe a virtual or live game to identify kicking, stopping and dribbling skills in football, Learners with postural defects or short stature could be appropriately positioned for comfort and clear view.

2. demonstrate in-step kick and outside of the foot kicking in football, Learners with postural defects could use alternative functional parts of the body, perform an alternative corresponding 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. observe a virtual or live game to identify kicking, stopping and dribbling skills in football, Learners with postural defects or short stature could be appropriately positioned for comfort and clear view.
2. demonstrate in-step kick and outside of the foot kicking in football, Learners with postural defects could use alternative functional parts of the body, perform an alternative corresponding 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Football together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Digital literacy: The learner operates digital devices to observe kicking, stopping and dribbling skills in Football.

● Creativity and imagination: The learner comes up with new ideas on how to improvise cones using papier mâché.

Values:
● Respect: The learner appreciates others’ effort as they execute the skills of kicking, shooting and dribbling.

● Responsibility: The learner observes safety precautions while executing skills and playing the mini Football game.

● Unity: The learner will cooperate to create cones and as they display team spirit as they play together

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Social cohesion- The learner plays together in two teams in a mini Football game.

● Resource mobilisation and utilisation- The learner seeks parental assistance when collecting materials for improvisation of

cones and colours using recyclable resources

Link to other learning areas:

Mathematics: The learner is exposed to ball trajectory as they practise kicking, stopping and dribbling.
